accepted.title: Measure-equivalence classes avoiding free subgroups
accepted.text: Does there exist a countable discrete nonamenable group Γ such that no countable group measure-equivalent to Γ contains a subgroup isomorphic to the nonabelian free group F₂? More strongly, can Γ be chosen torsion so that every countable group measure-equivalent to Γ is torsion? Two countable groups are measure-equivalent if they admit commuting, essentially free, measure-preserving actions on a nonzero standard σ-finite measure space, each action having a measurable fundamental domain of finite positive measure. A group is torsion if every element has finite order; nonamenable means it has no left-invariant mean on bounded functions.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.literature_finding: Gaboriau–Lyons and Bowen–Hoff–Ioana provide measurable embeddings or free orbit relations after an extension. These results do not produce a measure-equivalent whole group containing a free subgroup. No resolution of the entire measure-equivalence-class avoidance question was located in the dated primary scan.

accepted.title: Compactness from affine fixed points on Krein spaces
accepted.text: Let G be a Hausdorff topological group. Suppose every action of G by continuous affine automorphisms on any Hausdorff locally convex space E has a common fixed point whenever E has the Krein property and at least one orbit map g↦g·x is continuous. Must G be compact? The Krein property means that the closed convex hull of every compact subset of E is compact. No joint continuity of the action is required.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.literature_finding: The source proves compactness implies this fixed-point property, which implies precompactness; complete groups and groups measurable in their completion have positive results. The current primary scan found no extension covering every Hausdorff group, including incomplete groups.

accepted.title: Uniformly bounded affine actions on L-embedded spaces
accepted.text: Let E be an L-embedded Banach space: under its canonical inclusion in E^{**}, there is a closed subspace E_s with E^{**}=E⊕E_s and ‖x+y‖=‖x‖+‖y‖ for x∈E and y∈E_s. Let an abstract group G act on E by continuous affine automorphisms α_g(x)=π_gx+b_g, with sup_{g∈G}‖π_g‖<∞. If α_g(A)=A for every g and some bounded nonempty A⊂E, must there be x∈E fixed by every α_g?
accepted.subject: Functional Analysis & Operator Algebras
accepted.literature_finding: The isometric theorem of Bader–Gelander–Monod and the nonexpansive norm-distal extension of Wiśnicki are partial results. Equivalent renorming need not preserve L-embeddedness. These results do not settle the source’s general uniformly bounded affine-action question.

accepted.title: Closed subgroups of locally compact unitarizable groups
accepted.text: Call a Hausdorff topological group G unitarizable if every strongly continuous representation π:G→GL(H) on a complex Hilbert space with sup_g‖π(g)‖<∞ admits a bounded invertible S such that S⁻¹π(g)S is unitary for every g. If G is locally compact and unitarizable, must every closed subgroup of G, with its induced topology, be unitarizable? In particular, must G contain no subgroup isomorphic to F₂ that is discrete in the induced topology?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.literature_finding: Published Questions 36–37 retain the locally compact closed-subgroup and discrete-free-subgroup targets. Subgroup stability is already known for discrete groups. A current discrete Dixmier closure lead does not establish the corresponding result for all locally compact groups; no such full result was located.

accepted.title: Kazhdan and unitarizable locally compact groups
accepted.text: Call a Hausdorff topological group G unitarizable if every strongly continuous representation π:G→GL(H) on a complex Hilbert space with sup_g‖π(g)‖<∞ admits a bounded invertible S such that S⁻¹π(g)S is unitary for every g. If G is locally compact, unitarizable and has Kazhdan property (T), must it be compact? Property (T) means that every strongly continuous unitary representation π on a Hilbert space having almost invariant unit vectors has a nonzero invariant vector; almost invariance means that for every compact K⊂G and ε>0 there is a unit vector v with sup_{g∈K}‖π(g)v−v‖<ε.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.literature_finding: Amenability together with property (T) implies compactness. Unitarizability implying amenability for all locally compact groups would answer this question, but was not established by the bounded primary scan. A discrete-group closure claim does not automatically cover the source’s continuous locally compact representations.

accepted.title: The Krein property under the weak topology
accepted.text: Does there exist a Hausdorff locally convex space E such that the closed convex hull of every compact subset of E is compact in its original topology, but the same property fails for the weak topology σ(E,E′), where E′ is the continuous dual of the original topology?
accepted.subject: Functional Analysis & Operator Algebras
accepted.literature_finding: Krein’s theorem gives the property for the weak topology in quasi-complete spaces, so any counterexample here must be incomplete. The current primary scan found no result resolving the full comparison between the original and weak topologies.

excluded.reason: Closed by source reduction, independently checked by coordinator: take the nonamenable countable group affine Hilbert action π_gv+b_g with a bounded orbit and no fixed point from source Theorem5.2.21. Translate its bounded orbit to start at0, so {b_g} is bounded. On ℝ⊕H let T_g(t,v)=(t,π_gv+t b_g). Each T_g is a bounded invertible linear operator, T_gT_h=T_gh, and0 is fixed. A={(1,b_g)} is nonempty, bounded and invariant. Its closed convex hull is contained in {t=1}; any fixed point there would solve π_gv+b_g=v for every g, contrary to the original action. Taking the image of the group in GL(ℝ⊕H) gives the literal group-of-transformations formulation.
